title: Contentment with little
hookLine: a full cart that never checks out, and a one-sentence definition of wealth

lines: A CART THAT NEVER CHECKS OUT.
cards: An online cart, full, never checked out. A closet with the tags still on. A search at three in the morning for something nobody needed at noon.
Sometimes the wanting doesn't end when the package arrives; it moves on to the next thing. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, put a definition of wealth into one sentence.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase: richness isn't having a great many things; real richness is richness of the soul.

teach.h: NAFS: WEALTH MOVES INTO THE SELF.
teach.b: The word is qana'ah: contentment, being satisfied with what you've been given. The soul in the hadith is nafs, the same word this path has used for the self that wants and wants.
So the hadith moves wealth off the shelf and into the self. Two people can own exactly the same things. One feels poor, because the wanting runs ahead.
The other feels rich, because it doesn't.

But qana'ah isn't a vow to have nothing. In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet says, in paraphrase: successful is the one who has submitted, been given enough to live on, and been made content by Allah with what He gave. Enough.
Not nothing. A way to train it, also in Muslim, in paraphrase: look at those below you, not at those above you; that way you won't belittle Allah's blessings on you.

teach.h: LOOK DOWN THE LADDER, NOT UP.
teach.b: Look down the ladder, not up. A phone feed tends to run the other way. And a story of someone who missed it.
In surah al-Kahf, a man with two rich gardens walks into his own grounds and says he doesn't think any of this will ever perish.

teach.h: THE TWO GARDENS: MA SHA' ALLAH.
teach.b: His companion asks him, in paraphrase: when you entered your garden, why didn't you say, what Allah wills; there is no strength except in Allah? Ma sha' Allah.
You may hear it said over a new baby, a new house, a friend's success. It hands the good thing back to the One who gave it. Qana'ah is being able to stop at enough.

how: Muslims cultivate qana'ah by thanking Allah for what they have, saying ma sha' Allah over good things, and following the hadith's advice to look at those with less rather than those with more.

o: giving up every possession to live with nothing at all
saving carefully so you'll always have more than enough
contentment: being satisfied with enough of what you're given

p: al-Kahf: ma sha' Allah left unsaid

s: the hadith defines richness as owning a great deal
Bukhari: richness isn't many things; real richness is richness of the soul.
the successful one in Muslim's hadith is given enough to live on
submitted, given enough, and made content by Allah with what He gave.
the owner of the two gardens said ma sha' Allah when he walked in
his companion asks why he didn't say it.

games.q: a man walks into his two gardens, sure none of it will ever perish. his companion says there were words he should have said on the way in. what were they?
o: these are mine; I earned every one.
what Allah wills; there is no strength except in Allah.
nothing; it's better to stay quiet.
games.why: al-Kahf: ma sha' Allah, la quwwata illa billah. the words hand the gardens back to their Giver. he didn't say them, and the gardens were ruined.

practice: Choose one thing you already own and haven't really looked at in a while, a mug, a coat, a window, shoes that still work, and look at it the way you'd look at something just unwrapped.
Notice what it does for you every day without asking anything back. If you pray, you can say quietly, ma sha' Allah, or alhamdulillah; if not, just stay with the thing, and with the word enough.

wordCard.voice: Qana'ah. Contentment: richness of the soul, enough given and enough accepted, without the wanting running ahead. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: contentment, being satisfied with what one has.

carryVoice: Your line: rich in the soul. Enough, not nothing. That's today, done.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 6446 (richness is not abundance of goods but richness of the soul)
Sahih Muslim 1054 (successful: submitted, given enough, made content)
Sahih Muslim 2963 (look at those below you, not those above you)
Qur'an 18:32–42 (the two gardens; ma sha' Allah, la quwwata illa billah)
